research_question: Do heterogeneous software-engineering tasks exhibit enough composition-specific performance/cost variation that selecting the execution composition can improve the verified-success/cost frontier over the best fixed composition?
first_gate: Measure oracle composition headroom before building any adaptive composition selector.
null_hypothesis: The best fixed composition is economically equivalent to retrospective per-task oracle composition within the frozen scope.

initial_compositions.A3_PLAN_EXECUTE_VERIFY: planner plus executor plus independent verifier
initial_compositions.A4_PARALLEL_TWO_EXECUTORS_VERIFY: two parallel executor attempts plus independent selection/verification
initial_compositions.A5_ORCHESTRATOR_MANAGED: existing orchestrator-managed execution with frozen configuration

control_requirements: Hold task, model/capability budget, workspace, tools, permissions, acceptance criteria, and final verifier constant wherever technically feasible.
Record model/harness/tool differences explicitly when perfect control is impossible.
Do not infer architecture effects from comparisons that simultaneously change model capability without stratified analysis.
All composition overhead is included in total-system accounting.

headroom_analysis.oracle: For each task, retrospectively choose the lowest-total-cost verified-successful composition among frozen treatments.
headroom_analysis.baseline: Best fixed composition across the same task distribution.
headroom_analysis.decision: If OracleComposition is not materially better than BestFixedComposition, adaptive composition selection is rejected for this scope.

adaptive_selector: PROHIBITED in P3-A. A simple rule-based selector may be tested in P3-B only if P3-A demonstrates material oracle headroom.
anti_bias_rules: VERIFICATION is not assumed mandatory for every task
MAXIMAL composition is a baseline, not a preferred architecture
No new composition may be added post-hoc solely to rescue the DV hypothesis
holdout: Must be distinct/frozen before any architecture promotion claim
